papers.title: Magnetic excitons in a suspended 2D antiferromagnetic membrane
papers.authors: Joanna L. P. Wolff, Loïc Moczko, Jérémy Thoraval, Michelangelo Romeo, Benjamin Bacq-Labreuil, Stéphane Berciaud, Arnaud Gloppe
papers.abstract: Abstract Layered magnetic and strongly correlated materials, such as NiPS 3 , present a rich platform for condensed matter physics with intrinsic properties intertwined by magnetism and low-dimensionality. A suspended light-emitting 2D antiferromagnetic membrane forms a highly controllable hybrid system in which the interplay between spin ordering, optical and mechanical degrees of freedom can be uniquely explored. NiPS 3 hosts excitons responsible for a puzzling luminescence down to a few atomic layers, linked to its zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The exact nature of these excitons remains unclear. Here we report on the magnetic excitons of a suspended few-layer NiPS 3 membrane. We reveal nematic zigzag states and study the optical transitions induced by the magnon-mediated motion of the excitation in the magnetic lattice, resulting in magnon-dressed excitons. We observe a strain tuning of these emission lines, dependent on their microscopic origin, with rates that indicate a strong localization of the magnetic excitons, fading with the number of magnon-mediated hops.
papers.summary_en: This study investigates optical emission from suspended few-layer NiPS3, where excitons are associated with zigzag antiferromagnetic order. It reports nematic zigzag states and strain-dependent emission lines attributed to magnon-dressed magnetic excitons.

papers.title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites
papers.authors: Lulu Wang, Weixin He, Shurong Yuan, Chao Yang, Nihang Fu, Xinnan Peng, Kian Ping Loh, Pengfei Ou
papers.abstract: Abstract Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability. However, rational discovery remains difficult owing to uncertain phase formability and scarce, biased ferroelectric data. Here we show a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening. Starting from 11 known ferroelectric compounds in this family, symbolic regression defines a descriptor-bounded ferroelectric-consistent region. Similarity-guided expansion and chemical filtering reduce 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate divalent spacers, while machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation and connectivity analysis identify 338 candidates retaining Dion–Jacobson connectivity. Sequential prioritization by connectivity retention, chemical similarity, energetic refinement and synthetic accessibility selects s −2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine, leading to the synthesis of a PbI 4 -based Dion–Jacobson perovskite with experimentally confirmed ferroelectric switching. This prospective proof of concept shows how sparse property knowledge can be coupled with structural screening to prioritize organic spacer candidates for experimental synthesis.

papers.abstract: Altermagnets are a novel class of materials with unique momentum dependent spin-polarization of the electronic band structure, which opens up new avenues for spintronic devices. Altermagnetic α-MnTe is particularly interesting for such applications due to its giant spin splitting and the persistence of altermagnetic order up to room temperature. Growth of thin films is, however, challenging and governed by interactions with the substrate. As a result, the surface of α-MnTe thin films exhibits very different atomic structures in dependence of the substrate material. Whereas on SrF2(111) an atomically clean, perfectly (2x2) reconstructed surface forms, on InP(111)A the MnTe surface is always InTe terminated due to super-segregation of In from the substrate to the surface. Most strikingly, the InTe surfactant layer displays a quasi-periodic dislocation network to accommodate the InTe/MnTe lattice mismatch. This leads to the emergence of distinct surface states in dependence of surface termination that strongly affect the electronic band structure at the surface as shown by angle resolved photoemission and tunneling spectroscopy. Thus, control and characterization of the atomic structure of the surface is fundamentally important for understanding the properties of altermagnets and provides room for engineering and tailoring of spin-polarized states in actual devices.

papers.relevance_reason: The study connects substrate-controlled surface structure in an altermagnet to distinct spectroscopically observed surface states, providing a substantive result in quantum-materials physics.

papers.abstract: The $5d^5$ Ruddlesden-Popper iridates Sr$_2$IrO$_4$ and Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ have attracted considerable attention as spin-orbit entangled analogues of the cuprates, yet the origin of their antiferromagnetic insulating state, of Slater or of Mott-Heisenberg type, remains debated. We find that both materials sit in an intermediate regime in which itinerant and localized electrons cooperate in stabilizing the antiferromagnetic order, with Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ slightly more correlated than Sr$_2$IrO$_4$. We obtain this by computing, within dynamical mean-field theory, the interaction-temperature phase diagram of a realistic three-orbital $t_{2g}$ Hubbard model with spin-orbit coupling. Our study shows that neither the behavior of the gap across the Néel temperature nor the spin-polaron features of the spectral function unambiguously identify the cooperative regime, whereas the two-peak structure of the optical conductivity is reproduced only there and therefore constitutes a reliable fingerprint. By placing both compounds in a common phase diagram, our results reconcile seemingly contradictory experimental and theoretical reports, and provide a unified framework for future studies of the 214 iridates and of other spin-orbit coupled correlated materials.

papers.abstract: Every crystal surface breaks inversion symmetry even when the bulk is centrosymmetric, creating an intrinsic boundary polarity ($\mathbf{\mathit{P}}$). Here we show that this polarity enables zero-field nonreciprocal transport in the centrosymmetric kagome magnets TbMn$_6$Sn$_{6-x}$In$_x$. In symmetric TbMn$_6$Sn$_{4.4}$In$_{1.6}$ microdevices, opposing side surfaces exhibit second-harmonic longitudinal resistances of comparable magnitude and opposite sign. Reversing the spontaneous magnetization ($\mathbf{\mathit{M}}$) reverses both signals, whereas rotating $\mathbf{\mathit{M}}$ so that the toroidal moment $\mathbf{\mathit{P}} \times \mathbf{\mathit{M}}$ has no component along the current suppresses the response. In pristine TbMn$_6$Sn$_6$, the signal switches off across the spin-reorientation transition, providing a chemically ordered control of the same symmetry relation. Spatial potential mapping indicates that the nonlinear boundary contribution is distinct from the bulk linear conduction. Spin-orbit-coupled surface states associated with topological bands may enhance the effect. Crystal-surface polarity therefore offers a broadly applicable route to zero-field rectification in centrosymmetric magnetic conductors around room temperature.

papers.abstract: A gapped Dirac cone in antiferromagnetic topological insulators (AFM-TIs) is essential for realizing the quantized anomalous Hall effect, yet its intrinsic magnitude remains controversial. In the prototypical AFM-TI MnBi2Te4, however, the observed Dirac gap is significantly smaller than theoretical predictions or nearly absent, highlighting a long-standing discrepancy. Here we demonstrate that NdBi hosts a spin-polarized topological surface Dirac cone with a sizable gap of 17 meV at the Dirac point, in excellent agreement with density functional theory predictions (12 meV). This direct observation is enabled by high-resolution 7 eV laser-based spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, which unambiguously disentangles the spin-polarized surface Dirac cone from bulk-derived states. Furthermore, through temperature dependence and controlled surface contamination, we establish a direct linkage between surface magnetism and the Dirac gap, demonstrating that the gap opens only in the presence of surface magnetic order. papers.abstract: We establish an exact mechanism of magnetic confinement driven purely by kinetic frustration. In a finite open sawtooth $U=\infty$ Hubbard chain of $L$ unit cells doped with one hole, the ground state at magnetization $M$ contains $M$ polarized triplet dimers surrounding a connected singlet region of length $\ell_{\rm s}=L-M$. A magnetic field selects $M$ and hence the confinement length. The hole forms a standing wave in the singlet region with exponential tails in the triplet background. Confinement requires neither disorder nor an exchange-generated string tension: destructive interference between direct and apex-mediated hopping makes the triplet bonds reflecting. At $t_2/t_1=[2+4\cos(π/(\ell_{\rm s}+2))]^{-1/2}$, they become perfectly reflecting, producing a position-degenerate compact localized state. At every fixed field $0<h<h_{\rm sat}$, the singlet region remains finite as $L\to\infty$ and shrinks stepwise with increasing field, whereas at $h=0$ it spans the system.

papers.abstract: Nonlinear electrical transport enables the conversion and detection of electromagnetic signals, supporting wireless energy harvesting, sensing and frequency conversion. Achieving both a large response and electrical tunability remains a central materials challenge. Here we harness giant third-order nonlinearity to amplify and electrically control second-harmonic transport in the correlated polar metal Ca3Ru2O7. Superposing a dc bias on an ac excitation enhances the second-harmonic signal by more than an order of magnitude. The bias controls the polarity of the induced response and activates channels forbidden by symmetry at zero bias. Both transverse and longitudinal components scale quadratically with the ac excitation and are odd in the dc bias, with angular dependences consistent with third-order conductivity. The underlying third-harmonic electric-field responsivity reaches 4.5 \times 10-6 m2V-2 at 3 K, providing a quantitative measure of the strong nonlinearity. The induced response emerges below the spin-reorientation transition near 48 K, linking its enhancement to the reconstructed low-temperature electronic state. Theoretical calculations identify quantum-geometric contributions to the nonlinear conductivity and reproduce the observed response symmetry. These results demonstrate how strong higher-order nonlinearity can amplify an effective second-order response, providing a route to electrically tunable nonlinear transport in correlated materials.

papers.abstract: Finite-size effects are ubiquitous in quantum matter, yet typically invisible in the thermodynamic limit; when system size is restricted, boundaries and confinement reveal modified spectra, correlations, and emergent phenomena. With growing access to well-controlled few-spin systems, these effects are now directly observable and offer a route to probing universal physics and enabling quantum information applications. Here, we study finite-size physics in the quasi-one-dimensional Ising-like quantum antiferromagnet Ba(Co$_{1-x}$Mg$_x$)$_2$V$_2$O$_8$ with $x = 2\%$ and $x = 5\%$, where non-magnetic Mg$^{2+}$ ions fragment the Co$^{2+}$ spin chains into finite segments. Combining inelastic neutron scattering and numerical calculations, we identify distinct regimes with fundamentally different low-energy quantum excitations: spinons confined to chain boundaries, and a cluster mode in shorter chains corresponding to a collective reversal of the Néel-ordered segment without classical analogue. Our results demonstrate how chemical substitution acts as a quantum microscope providing direct access to boundary-shaped excitations in strongly correlated spin systems.

papers.abstract: We investigate spinon--spinon interactions in the quasi-one-dimensional $S=1/2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet Cu(C$_4$H$_4$N$_2$)(NO$_3$)$_2$ (CuPzN) using inelastic neutron scattering. papers.abstract: When electrons move through non-trivial spin textures in magnetic metals, conduction electrons couple to magnetic order through both their charge and their spin, acquiring non-trivial equations of motion and a dynamic spin polarization providing the foundation of spintronics. These mechanisms are, however, almost invariably reciprocal and the resistance a current encounters does not depend on its flow direction. Here we show that a chiral crystal lattice and an independently reversible chiral magnetic order together produce a diode whose forward direction is set by the magnetism rather than by the structure. In the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet Co$_{1/3}$TaS$_2$, whose chiral lattice hosts a chiral magnetic order of its own, independent handedness, we observe a pronounced nonreciprocal resistance. Unlike conventional electrical magnetochiral anisotropy, which is driven by an external magnetic field, our spontaneous magnetic diode effect arises from an internal noncoplanar spin texture with vanishing net magnetization. Symmetry analysis and model calculations show that the effect originates from the interplay of noncoplanar spin order and spin-orbit coupling, which generates a chiral, time-reversal-symmetry-breaking electronic response. Crucially, reversing the magnetic handedness reverses the sign of the nonreciprocal resistance, demonstrating magnetic control of the diode polarity.
papers.physics_advance: A noncoplanar antiferromagnetic texture and spin-orbit coupling produce a spontaneous magnetic diode response whose polarity reverses with magnetic handedness, without net magnetization or an applied field.

papers.abstract: We investigate the $1/9$ magnetization plateau of the spin-$1/2$ kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet using infinite projected entangled-pair states and identify a spin-density-wave state with a $27$-site unit cell and a lower variational energy than previous approaches. In contrast to higher-magnetization plateaus, which are well described by localized magnons on nonoverlapping hexagons and preserve a sixfold rotational symmetry, the $1/9$ plateau only keeps a threefold rotational symmmetry and consists of a tiling by three types of $9$-site clusters related by $\pm2π/3$ rotations. These conclusions are supported by a complementary cluster mean-field theory which correctly preserves the symmetry of the higher plateaus but leads to the same spontaneous symmetry breaking for the $1/9$ plateau with a qualitatively similar pattern of nine different local magnetizations.

papers.abstract: The spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet (AFM) provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing quantum spin-liquid (QSL) and magnetization-plateau states. Experimental progress, however, has been hindered by structural disorder, whose effects on these quantum states remain elusive. A key experimental challenge is therefore to connect intrinsic and disorder-dominated regimes through controlled disorder and identify emergent degrees of freedom associated with disorder. Here we introduce controlled point defects through electron irradiation into the spin-1/2 kagome AFM YCu3(OH)6.5Br2.5 (YCOB) and track the resulting evolution of its low-energy magnetic states. High-field magnetic torque measurements reveal that the 1/9 and 1/3 magnetization plateaus are strongly suppressed by only ~0.05% irradiation-induced defects, demonstrating that these delicate quantum many-body states are extraordinarily fragile against dilute disorder. Moreover, the irradiation induces a sign reversal of the magnetic torque only at low temperatures and low fields, indicating the emergence of correlated defect-induced moments rather than isolated free spins. Remarkably, the characteristic scaling of the magnetic specific heat, absent in pristine YCOB, progressively emerges with increasing disorder. These findings establish dilute disorder as an effective tuning parameter that drives the kagome AFM from intrinsic quantum states toward a disorder-dominated regime. The contrasting responses further identify pristine YCOB as an exceptionally clean kagome AFM for accessing intrinsic quantum states.

papers.authors: Samir Lounis
papers.summary_en: The authors derive field-linear three-spin interactions from a microscopic electronic Hamiltonian, distinguishing isotropic terms that do not require spin-orbit coupling from relativistic terms that do. They identify consequences for magnetic trimers and continuum chiral textures, including a field-dependent Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.

papers.abstract: Magnetic fields are commonly incorporated in atomistic spin models through the Zeeman energy of individual magnetic moments. Starting from a microscopic electronic Hamiltonian, we show that the Zeeman coupling of conduction electrons also generates field-linear three-spin interactions, the lowest-order corrections allowed by time-reversal symmetry. Using a Green-function expansion of the grand potential, we identify two classes of interactions. Isotropic terms of the form $(\mathbf S_i\cdot\mathbf S_j)(\mathbf S_k\cdot\mathbf B)$ exist without spin-orbit coupling, and their total strength obeys a sum rule involving the three-site electronic loop at the Fermi energy. Relativistic terms require spin-orbit coupling and include $\mathbf K_{ijk}\cdot\mathbf B,χ_{ijk}$, where $χ_{ijk}=\mathbf S_i\cdot(\mathbf S_j\times\mathbf S_k)$ is the scalar spin chirality. We show that this coupling is forbidden in the spin channel without spin-orbit coupling, whereas the orbital channel recovers the orbital-flux mechanism of Mott insulators. Exact diagonalization of the Hubbard trimer confirms the independence and additivity of both channels. For magnetic trimers in Rashba electron gases, we derive analytical expressions showing that $\mathbf K_{ijk}$ lies in-plane at first order in spin-orbit coupling but vanishes for $C_{3v}$-symmetric trimers, where an out-of-plane component emerges at second order. These interactions can shift magnetization-step fields and modify field-induced noncoplanarity. In the continuum limit, the chirality coupling splits skyrmions from antiskyrmions, while the relativistic terms generate a field-dependent Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.

papers.relevance_reason: This microscopic theory establishes new field-induced interactions in magnetic systems and predicts their consequences for noncoplanarity and skyrmion energetics.

In Rashba systems, the vector Kᵢⱼₖ lies in-plane at first order in spin-orbit coupling but vanishes for C₃ᵥ-symmetric trimers; an out-of-plane component appears at second order. The authors further find that these interactions can shift magnetization-step fields and alter field-induced noncoplanarity, while the continuum chirality coupling splits skyrmions from antiskyrmions.

papers.abstract: Stabilizing two-dimensional superconductivity in a bulk superconducting material provides a unique route to exploring the interplay between superconducting condensates of different dimensionalities. Here, we present evidence for a distinct surface-associated superconducting state in Pb-substituted NiBi$_3$. NiBi$_{2.8}$Pb$_{0.2}$ exhibits a resistive onset at $T_{c,\mathrm{onset}}^{*}\approx8.1$~K, nearly twice the bulk superconducting transition temperature of approximately 4.1~K. The absence of a corresponding Meissner response or specific-heat anomaly at the higher-temperature transition supports its non-bulk origin. A cusp-like angular dependence of the critical field, well described by the two-dimensional Tinkham model, together with nonlinear current--voltage characteristics and signatures of a Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless transition, establishes the low-dimensional character of this superconducting state. Remarkably, the surface-associated superconductivity persists well beyond the bulk upper critical field, reaching a maximum ratio of $H_{c3}/H_{c2}\approx4.3$, far exceeding the conventional Saint-James--de Gennes value of 1.695. These results demonstrate that Pb substitution can stabilize an anomalously enhanced low-dimensional superconducting state in NiBi$_3$, providing a platform for investigating superconductivity at the boundary of a bulk superconductor.

papers.authors: Ke Wang
papers.summary_en: The authors investigate whether correlations that promote Wigner crystallization in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene can also drive superconductivity in the neighboring metallic regime.
papers.summary: Can the correlations favoring electron crystallization also generate superconductivity in the neighboring metal? papers.abstract: Can the correlations favoring electron crystallization also generate superconductivity in the neighboring metal? We investigate this possibility in rhombohedral tetralayer graphene with repulsive Coulomb interactions. Self-consistent Hartree--Fock calculations identify a commensurate triangular Wigner-crystal state. To investigate pairing on the metallic side, we construct a crossing-symmetric particle--hole vertex using coupled parquet and Bethe--Salpeter equations, incorporating exchange vertex corrections beyond polarization-bubble screening. Near crystallization, the enhanced electronic correlations generate an effective attraction favoring chiral $f$-wave pairing. Superconductivity is confined to a narrow metallic region adjacent to the crystal, qualitatively consistent with the superconducting sleeve observed near an insulating regime in rhombohedral graphene. These results connect the emergence of chiral pairing and its location in the phase diagram to the electronic correlations favoring crystallization.

papers.abstract: The Josephson effect provides a direct phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order and has played a central role in identifying unconventional pairing symmetries1-6. Conventional Josephson interferometry, however, extracts phase information through engineered junction geometries and crystallographic orientations, rather than by resolving the internal phase structure of the pair state within a single unit cell. Here, we use a superconducting Nb tip to realize atomic-scale Josephson interferometry in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3. Despite a fully gapped quasiparticle spectrum, the local Josephson response exhibits a striking intra-unit-cell pattern, with maxima centred on Fe-Fe bonds and robust nodal lines along the Fe-Se directions. We show that these nodal lines arise from destructive interference between Josephson tunnelling amplitudes associated with opposite-sign pairing components. Microscopic calculations reproduce the observed spatial pattern and identify it as a fingerprint of nodeless d-wave pairing. Our results establish intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry as a local phase-sensitive probe of pairing symmetry in unconventional superconductors.

papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent measurement of high-temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate system La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ in the bulk as well as thin film samples, we seek to understand the role of the interlayer coupling in this system in dictating the pairing symmetry. Many proposals posit the existence of an $s_\pm$ superconducting phase in close competition with the mroe conventional cuprate-like $d$-wave state in both weak- and strong-coupling theories. However, at least in the latter, the effects of Coulomb repulsion and the double occupancy constraint have been largely neglected. In this manuscript, we propose a mean-field fractionalization treatment that captures the full $SU(2)$ particle-hole symmetry of the t-J model at half-filling, and show how a systematic treatment of this new symmetry leads to an added Coulomb pseudopotential constraint - one that is absent in the usual $U(1)$ treatment. We then apply this new fractionalization scheme to a simplified bilayer t-J model of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, showing how the Coulomb pseudopotential suppresses the existence of $s_\pm$ symmetry in favor of $d$-wave pairing.

papers.abstract: The Little-Parks effect played a pivotal role in establishing fluxoid quantization in doubly connected superconductors and providing early evidence for electron pairing, central to BCS theory. More recently, it has emerged as an important phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order. Yet the amplitude of the Little-Parks oscillation has never been fully understood theoretically, as the conventional mean-field Ginzburg-Landau description does not account for its pronounced temperature dependence. Here, we develop a universal theoretical framework incorporating thermal fluctuations in reduced-dimensional superconducting rings. By analyzing Little-Parks measurements across multiple superconductors, we show that the resulting scaling quantitatively captures the temperature-dependent oscillation amplitudes over a broad range of materials and device geometries, resolving the long-standing discrepancy between theory and experiment.

papers.abstract: Odd-parity spin splitting constrains magnetic band crossings but does not determine their topological descendants. We show that the Chern contribution of an isolated inverted sector is controlled by the phase winding of its transverse mass pair: when the masses and tangential velocities reverse together, contributions from successive Dirac points add rather than cancel. This distinguishes topological winding from the polynomial degree labeling the magnetic parent. For specified complementary masses, periodic tetragonal $h$- and hexagonal $j$-wave models host eight and twelve same-chirality Weyl points on a momentum plane, with gapped-slice Chern numbers $|C|=4$ and $6$, respectively. A microscopic four-band $p$-wave model identifies an antiunitary obstruction to first-order transverse masses and demonstrates a symmetry-broken $C=1$ phase at quarter filling. First-principles calculations for the proposed coplanar spin-vortex texture of LaMnAu$_5$ reveal the $h$-wave nodal pattern, its anisotropic spin--orbit reconstruction, and a mirror-channel spectral response that reverses under opposite spin rotations. Together, these results distinguish the symmetry of an odd-parity magnetic parent from the mass structure controlling the topology of its descendants.

papers.abstract: The relevance of spin, lattice and orbital degrees of freedom in the quasi-2D Ising-like magnet Li$_2$FeSiO$_4$ is demonstrated by thermal expansion and specific heat measurements supported by numerical studies. By means of thermodynamic and Grüneisen analysis, we separate the orbital signatures and quantify the energy gap and its pressure dependence from the experimental data as $Δ\sim 300 - 350$ K and $\partial \ln Δ/\partial p_{\rm c} \approx -4.6$ %/GPa). Both values excellently agree with the theoretical DFT predictions. The thermal expansion anomalies associated with the onset of long-range magnetic order imply significant magneto-elastic coupling and are used to determine the anisotropic uniaxial strain dependencies of $T_{\rm N}$. They are dominated by the in-plane (i.e., $c$ axis) response $(\partial \ln{ T_{\rm N}} )/\partial p_{\rm c} \simeq 15$ %/GPa while the (negative) $a$ axis and (positive) out-of-plane ($b$ axis) pressure dependencies are much smaller. Short-range magnetic order extends well above $T_{\rm N}$ but is not driven by the same energy scale as $T_{\rm N}$ as evidenced by the observation of non-monotonic in-plane distortion, sign-change of the Grüneisen parameter, and failure of Grüneisen scaling.

papers.abstract: In Ni-Mn-based Heusler alloys, the magnetocaloric effect originates from a first-order magnetostructural transition (FOMST). However, the influence of particle and grain size on thermal hysteresis, transition width, and nucleation and growth mechanism remains poorly understood, as mechanical grinding can introduce residual stresses and processing-induced defects. In this study, we examined the size dependence of the FOMST in gas-atomized Ni-Mn-Sn powder by combining microstructural characterization with temperature-dependent XRD, magnetometry, calorimetry and single-particle measurements, enabling decoupling of size dependence from processing-related influences. We observed a pronounced size dependence of the transition ranges (Ms-Mf) and (Af-As), which decrease with decreasing particle size and approach zero for single-crystalline particles below ~20-30 micrometer. The thermal hysteresis decreases with increasing particle size, reaching a lower limit of 17 K for large polycrystalline particles above 100 micrometer. EBSD reveals a nearly constant grain size, implying a transition from polycrystalline to single-crystalline particles as particle size decreases. In polycrystalline particles, multiple grains transform gradually over an extended temperature interval because grain boundaries act as barriers to the progression of transformation. In contrast, single-grain particles lack preferred nucleation sites, resulting in larger hysteresis, while the absence of barriers to transformation propagation causes the entire particle to transform in a narrow range. These results demonstrate that the size dependence of the FOMST is governed by the interplay between particle size, grain boundaries, and the free particle surface.

papers.abstract: Geometrical flat bands provide an ideal platform for studying electronic correlations and quantum-geometric effects. Although the ferromagnetic Weyl semimetal \CoSnS is generally considered a moderately correlated system, recent spectroscopy experiments have revealed a flat-band feature near the Fermi level ($\EF$) that is absent in conventional density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Using DFT plus dynamical mean-field theory and a minimal kagome model, we show that this feature arises not from heavy-fermion-like dynamical band renormalization, but from the shifting of a $d_{x^2-y^2}$ dominated geometrical kagome flat band toward $\EF$ driven by orbital- and spin-dependent self-energies. The relocated flat band enhances the local Berry curvature near $\EF$, resulting in a strongly energy-dependent anomalous Hall conductivity and a giant anomalous Nernst effect. Our findings establish an orbital-selective correlation mechanism for positioning geometrical flat bands at $\EF$, and propose anomalous thermoelectric transport as a sensitive probe of flat band induced topology.
